The Holy Michael Cathedral, or the Church of the Archangel Michael, is the main Orthodox shrine in Izhevsk and the cathedral of the Izhevsk Diocese. The church is located on Krasnaya (Mikhailovskaya) Square, one of the highest points in the city. It can be seen from almost any part of Izhevsk, as it stands at a height of 67 meters.
Church of the Kazan Icon of the Mother of God
The Church of the Kazan Icon of the Mother of God is an Orthodox church in Izhevsk, the base of the Diocesan Department of Education and Religious Catechesis of the Izhevsk and Udmurt Diocese.

The museum was founded in November 1920 in accordance with the resolution of the Executive Committee of the Izhevsk City Council as the Izhevsk Museum of Local History. The founder and first director of the museum was A. M. Filippov, a veterinarian who worked part-time at the museum.

"Friendship of Peoples" (also known as "Forever with Russia" and popularly referred to as "Kulakovas Skis") is a monument in Izhevsk dedicated to the 400th anniversary of Udmurtia's incorporation into Russia.

The Alexander Nevsky Cathedral is an Orthodox church in Izhevsk. It belongs to the Izhevsk Diocese of the Russian Orthodox Church. In 1994-2017, it was the cathedral of the diocese. The cathedral was built in 1823, modeled after the St. Andrews Cathedral in Kronstadt (designed by architect Andreyan Zakharov). It became an important part of the classical architecture of the Vyatka Province. It was originally planned as the central church of the Izhevsk factory. In 1929, the church was looted and closed, and later served as a cinema called "Koloss". In 1990, with the active participation of Bishop Palladius (who was the rector from 1990 to 1992), it was returned to the Russian Orthodox Church.
